title: Redesign Mission lines as reversible checkbox workflow
description: Replace the flaky current/history positional editor with explicit one-line Mission items that can be completed and revived, preserve human-authored text, and remove abandoned empty insertions.
design: Persist active and completed missions as separate canonical Mission/Mission history sections. Normalize legacy positional rows on load. Add per-workspace transient history fold state; Enter toggles it. Mission x/X moves rows between sections, Mission dd is a no-op, and o creates a provisional human row removed on empty Esc. Regen preserves [h] rows/history and deterministically deduplicates similar agent rows.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Active Mission contains one-line checkbox-style items and supports multiple simultaneous missions. 2. X on an active mission completes it into folded Mission history; X on a revealed history item revives it into active Mission. 3. Mission history is folded by default and can be explicitly unfolded/folded without reordering unrelated rows. 4. o in active Mission inserts a new human mission; Esc removes it if it remains empty. 5. Human missions are marked [h], never model-edited, and regenerated agent missions are deduplicated against semantically similar human missions. 6. Existing task/Beads X and o behavior is unchanged. 7. Full tests, release build, and live cmux Mission workflow pass.
notes: Implemented explicit active/history Mission state, reversible x/X completion, Enter fold, Mission dd no-op, provisional o with empty-Esc cancellation, [h] preservation, deterministic agent deduplication, and completed-work non-revival. Verification: scoped rustfmt/diff checks, cargo clippy --all-targets (existing warnings only), cargo build, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build --release, and isolated live cmux Release smoke all passed.
close_reason: Implemented, fully tested, and verified in an isolated live Release workflow.

title: Resolve tracker from workspace identity and group Linear by feature
description: A workspace's title or description may identify an Olympus platform feature even when the focused cwd points elsewhere. Resolve the registered project/feature from that workspace identity, honor the resolved unit's tracker, and segment Linear list rows by feature name.
acceptance_criteria: Title and description can independently resolve an Olympus feature; resolved feature tracker overrides incidental cwd; ambiguous evidence degrades conservatively; Linear list view groups projected issues by feature name; full tests, release build, and live Olympus workspace validation pass.
close_reason: Implemented identity-first tracker resolution and Linear feature segmentation; 630 tests passed, release built, and live group-graders/trace-viewer verification passed.

title: Keep Mission non-empty from human or conversation intent
description: Mission regen can leave ## Mission empty. Preserve human-authored Mission text as the primary source; when no human Mission exists, synthesize one or more very short bullets from the workspace conversation summaries. Add regression coverage and validate live.
design: Post-LLM Mission reconciliation order: preserve non-empty saved Mission; otherwise accept non-empty generated Mission; repair empty generated Mission from latest user ask, then recent user explanation, then up to three session/surface summaries, then a short workspace fallback. Empty Mission is also a scheduler trigger even with zero pending events.
acceptance_criteria: Human-authored Mission survives regen as primary content; empty Mission falls back to concise conversation-derived bullets; generated Mission never remains empty when useful conversation context exists; full tests and release build pass.
notes: Validated with 5 new regression behaviors, full single-threaded suite, release build, clippy, CLI smokes, forced live regen of empty mc workspace, and automatic zero-event regen of empty obsidian workspace.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic non-empty Mission reconciliation and automatic empty-Mission regen scheduling. Saved human Mission remains authoritative; fallbacks are concise and capped. Full suite, release, and two live cmux paths passed.

title: Add locally selectable OpenAI short-text provider
description: Mission Control currently uses xAI for workspace prefixes, remote intent extraction, and per-surface overall summaries. Add an equivalent OpenAI Responses API provider selected by machine-local config, load its key from explicit config or the reflectionai GCP secret, configure ref for OpenAI, and surface configuration/secret failures as a non-fatal global TUI warning.
design: Add machine-local JSON config at ~/data/mission-control/config.json with short_text_provider (xai default, openai opt-in). Refactor the three short generations behind one concrete provider client; the selected provider is authoritative rather than silently falling through. Use OpenAI Responses API with gpt-5.4-mini and extract output_text from response output items. Resolve OpenAI credentials only when needed, with explicit flag/env precedence and bounded gcloud execution. Render sanitized credential/config failures in the global info layer. Configure ref locally for OpenAI.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All three xAI-backed short-text operations can run through the provider selected in ~/data/mission-control/config.json.
2. short_text_provider accepts xai or openai; missing config preserves xAI, and invalid config is surfaced without crashing.
3. On ref, local config selects openai; only the selected provider is called, with existing deterministic/no-result degradation on failure.
4. OPENAI_API_KEY/--openai-api-key wins; otherwise, when OpenAI is selected, mc runs gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=OPENAI_API_KEY_AGENTIC --project=reflectionai without persisting or logging the key.
5. A failed/empty/timed-out gcloud lookup does not prevent mc from starting and produces a persistent global warning in the TUI info layer.
6. Provider/config/API/secret/warning tests pass, the full single-threaded suite passes, live mc launches, and cargo build --release succeeds without warning-budget regression.
close_reason: Implemented and validated selectable OpenAI short-text provider, gcloud key lookup, and global warning

title: Clamp Mission cursor to visible history
description: Boyan reports that pressing j/k in Mission history can move the cursor into hidden Mission-history rows below the fold, making the highlight disappear. Clamp Mission navigation to the rendered active Mission plus visible history rows for now.
design: Move the visible Mission history cap into trajectory data as a shared cursor/render limit. Use that limit in trajectory_view rendering and trajectory_edit cursor helpers so hidden Mission rows are not reachable by j/k for now.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist: Mission navigation treats only the active Mission row plus rendered history rows as cursor-reachable; pressing j at the last visible Mission history row moves to the next section instead of hidden Mission rows; pressing k from the next section lands on the last visible Mission history row, not a hidden row; G/other cross-section helpers do not target hidden Mission rows; renderer and navigator share one visible Mission item limit; tests cover the clamp; cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build --release, git diff --check, and live/manual smoke where feasible pass.
notes: Implemented shared Mission visible cap so navigation cannot move into hidden Mission history rows. Added tests for j from last visible Mission history, k from next section, and G in Mission-only docs. Verified: cargo test visible_mission -- --test-threads=1; cargo test -- --test-threads=1; cargo build; cargo build --release; git diff --check. Live surface readback shows one active Mission row, 12 visible history rows, and hidden parked count.
close_reason: Fixed Mission cursor navigation to share the renderer's visible history cap and skip hidden rows.

title: Make Detail navigation stable for l and j/k
description: Boyan reports Detail is flaky: pressing l from Detail can jump directly into a surface, and j/k no longer consistently show highlighted trajectory cursor movement. Fix Detail key ownership so l does not switch/open surfaces from Detail and j/k reliably initialize/show the cursor highlight.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist: pressing l in trajectory-backed Detail does not switch to/open a cmux surface; l is either a no-op or an editor-owned key in Detail; j/k in trajectory-backed Detail initialize/preserve edit_state and produce a visible nav cursor highlight; j/k does not mutate detail_scroll; PageUp/PageDown and mouse wheel still scroll Detail; tests cover l routing and j/k visible cursor state; cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build --release, git diff --check, and live cmux smoke pass.
notes: Fixed Detail navigation flakiness. l/Right now only open Detail from the sidebar and no-op in Detail, so they cannot fall through to cmux workspace selection during trajectory load races. Trajectory-backed Detail now initializes edit_state/cursor as soon as it is focused, and opening Detail resets detail_scroll to keep the cursor highlight on-screen. The trajectory router also owns l/Right when a trajectory is loaded. Verified focused tests, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build, cargo build --release, git diff --check, and live cmux smoke: l from Detail stayed in Detail, j/k stayed in Detail without viewport scroll.
close_reason: Fixed Detail key ownership and cursor initialization: l/Right only open Detail from Sidebar and no-op in Detail, trajectory-backed Detail eagerly initializes the nav cursor and resets scroll on open, and l/Right are consumed by the trajectory router when loaded. Verified focused tests, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build, cargo build --release, git diff --check, and live cmux smoke on workspace:2/surface:2.

title: Preserve j/k cursor navigation while Detail scrolls
description: Boyan clarified that j/k in mc Detail should continue moving the trajectory cursor; scrolling support must not steal those editor navigation keys. Keep mouse wheel/detail scrolling working without breaking cursor movement.
design: Remove the plain Detail key-scroll shortcut for j/k/arrows before the trajectory editor router. Keep mouse wheel handling at the top of the event loop. Use tests on routing helpers and live cmux smoke to prevent regression.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist: j/k in Detail nav mode reaches the trajectory editor and moves the cursor; j/k no longer mutates detail_scroll directly; mouse wheel still mutates detail_scroll in plain Detail view; entering edit mode on Mission does not expand all historical Mission bullets back into the active detail view; insert/peek/dispatch modes keep intended routing; tests cover j/k cursor routing, mouse scroll routing, and Mission condensation while editing; cargo test -- --test-threads=1 and cargo build --release pass; live cmux surface verifies j/k cursor movement, mouse wheel scrolling, and no Mission-history explosion after Enter/edit.
notes: Implemented Detail routing correction: j/k and arrows now fall through to the trajectory editor cursor path; PageUp/PageDown and mouse wheel remain the Detail viewport scroll inputs. Mission rendering stays condensed even in insert/edit mode, so Enter/edit does not expand all historical Mission bullets. Footer now reflects trajectory-backed Detail behavior as j/k cursor, Enter/i edit/act, pg/wheel scroll. Verified with focused tests, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build, cargo build --release, git diff --check, and live cmux smoke on workspace:2 surface:2.
close_reason: Fixed Detail input ownership: j/k/arrows remain trajectory cursor navigation while PageUp/PageDown and mouse wheel scroll Detail. Mission view now renders one active Mission bullet plus capped Mission history even during edit/insert, preventing the Enter/edit explosion. Footer now labels trajectory-backed Detail correctly. Verified by focused routing/render tests, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build, cargo build --release, git diff --check, and live cmux smoke on workspace:2 surface:2.

title: Remove 60s hook_status staleness window
description: agent_state() only trusts hook_status if <60s old. State only changes on hook events, so absence of events = unchanged state. Make last hook verdict authoritative until next event.
close_reason: agent_state(): removed 60s hook_status freshness gate; last hook verdict authoritative until next event. Build clean, 230 tests pass.

title: Self-healing cmux event subscriber (respawn + reap orphans)
description: subscribe() is fire-and-forget; if the cmux events child dies, mc silently loses hook updates until restart. Wrap in respawn loop with capped backoff. Reap orphaned subscribers on startup + kill_on_drop (DONE in events.rs).
close_reason: events.rs: reap orphans (pkill -f) before spawn + kill_on_drop(true); main.rs respawn loop w/ capped backoff. Cleared 9 live orphans. Build clean.

title: Hooks-first agent state: local→hooks, remote→typesafe

Also reaped orphan cmux-events subscribers (kill_on_drop + startup pkill).

title: mc fights blueprint histories layout: histories must live in ~/agents (Obsidian vault), not ~/data/Sessions
description:
TUI fails to load session data with: 'histories dir validation failed: ~/agents/histories points to .../Obsidian/Agents/Sessions, expected ~/data/Sessions'.

Root cause: mc hardcodes ~/data/Sessions as the canonical session-log store and even migrates the blueprint symlink away from the vault, contradicting the agents blueprint where ~/agents/histories -> obs/Agents/Sessions is canonical (541 real logs there vs 1 in ~/data/Sessions). Secondary bug: prompts::obsagents_root() and summarize::output_dir() fall back to a nonexistent ~/agents/Obsidian symlink instead of the real ~/agents/obsAgents.

Decision (Boyan): align mc to blueprint. Relax validate_histories_dir to dir+readable; stop setup.rs creating ~/data/Sessions and migrating the histories symlink; remove session_logs_dir; fix obsagents_root/output_dir fallbacks to ~/agents/obsAgents; update smoke tests. Release build + verify.
close_reason: Aligned mc to the agents blueprint. validate_histories_dir now just checks dir+readable (trusts the blueprint symlink); setup.rs no longer creates ~/data/Sessions or repoints ~/agents/histories (warns if missing); removed paths::session_logs_dir; fixed obsagents_root()/summarize::output_dir() fallbacks from nonexistent ~/agents/Obsidian to ~/agents/obsAgents. Updated 4 smoke tests (2 setup, 1 inverted migrate->preserve, 1 inverted backfill fail->accept). Verified: release backfill-window succeeds against the real vault-backed ~/agents/histories (5 workspaces/17 surfaces); setup leaves the blueprint symlink untouched. 224 bin + 11 smoke tests pass single-threaded (1 pre-existing parallel-race test unrelated).

title: Reap orphan cmux events subscribers on mc restart
description: A SIGKILLed/crashed mc leaves its long-lived 'cmux events --reconnect --category agent --no-heartbeat' child orphaned (reparented to launchd); each restart stacked another. Reap by exact-argv pkill -f before spawning, and kill_on_drop(true) so graceful shutdown takes the child with it.
close_reason: Implemented in src/cmux/events.rs: EVENTS_ARGS shared slice, reap_orphan_subscribers() via pkill -f exact argv before spawn, kill_on_drop(true) on the child. Release build passes.

title: Consume centralized mux protocol state (~/data/mux) instead of dedicated agent hooks
description: Boyan directive (2026-06-09): agents' native hooks feed ONE centralized PROTOCOL store — ~/data/mux/sessions/<session_id>.json (working flag, last_event, turn_count, prompt/turn timestamps; locked single-writer 'arcmux hook') plus per-session JSONL under ~/data/mux/hook-output/. The dir is deliberately protocol-named (mux), not app-named: arcmux is today's producer but the contract is the files. Contract doc: ~/Projects/arcmux/docs/state-dir.md (~/data/arcmux/ is arcmux-private and NOT part of the contract). mission-control should read ~/data/mux for agent-activity facts (working/idle, last turn end, turn counts) instead of registering its own claude/codex hooks where the data overlaps. Scope: (1) inventory what mission-control-hook.sh collects (workspace_id ↔ session-file stamping) vs what mux state provides; (2) consume mux state for overlapping facts; (3) keep a hook ONLY for non-overlapping facts, or extend the mux session env/state to carry them and drop the hook entirely. Same migration applies to cmux.app's hook bridges (separate effort, no checkout here).
acceptance_criteria: mission-control derives agent working/idle + turn timing from ~/data/mux/sessions/*.json (poll or fswatch); any retained hook is justified in a comment as non-overlapping; net hook count for mission-control purposes decreases; verified against a live mux-spawned claude and grok session.
close_reason: Shipped mux-state reader for ~/data/mux/sessions JSON, wired WorkspaceState mux_status polling via cmux session_id->workspace_id mapping, removed hook-event/session-frontmatter status derivation, documented retained mc bind/session-history hook as non-overlapping, and added fixture tests for claude/grok-style mux state because no current live mux-spawned claude/grok session docs were running (only stale 2026-06-04 docs present). Verified: cargo build warnings 2 <= baseline 10; cargo test -- --test-threads=1 green; cargo build --release green; release CLI --help/resolve/setup green; global mc --help green; live mc TUI launched and exited with q.

title: Mute 'command finished' notifications (zero-signal noise)
description: All notifications that just say a command/tool finished are pure noise — 0 signal to Boyan. Suppress them entirely. Keep only meaningful notifications (agent needs input, error/failure, blocked, done-with-result). Audit notification sources (cmux hook events Notification/Stop, agentLifecycle transitions, mc-emitted notifications) and drop the 'completed'/'command finished' class.
notes: AUDIT (2026-06-10): mission-control emits NO OS notifications — no osascript/terminal-notifier/notification call exists anywhere in src/. mc only READS mux_status.last_event (== 'notification' → AgentState::NeedsMe) for in-TUI state. The 'command finished' notifications come from the arcmux/cmux hook daemon (arcmux hook on Notification/Stop), NOT this repo. So haw cannot be implemented in mission-control as written — the suppression belongs in arcmux's hook→notification path. Recommend re-homing this ticket to arcmux.
close_reason: Misfiled — mission-control emits no OS notifications (audit confirmed: no osascript/terminal-notifier/notification call in src/). The 'command finished' notifications are fired by arcmux's hook->notify path (internal/manager/cmuxcli/notify.go). Re-homed to arcmux-wdk.
